Priya to provide sample Terraform VPC template + ingress/egress baseline (by 2026-10-02)

summary: Deep dive on Redwood Private (VPC) security architecture focused on network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling and shared responsibility. Customer requested SOC2/ISO documents, sample VPC templates, and a connectivity test. Discussed KMS/HSM integration, audit log forwarding (SIEM), RBAC/SSO integration, and options for air-gapped on-prem deployment.
topics: Audit logs, retention and SIEM forwarding
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. Priya is our security / infra SE. Carlos is taking notes. how's everyone?
[00:12] Mark Thompson: Hi yeah thanks. Mark here, head of security at Silver Lake Finance. we have Elena our cloud architect, Samir our CISO, and Jill on the network side.
[00:25] Priya Nanduri: great, i'll kick off with a high level of the private deployment - think of it as a customer-owned VPC where we deploy Redwood runtime components into your account or into a customer-managed VPC in your region. we try to minimize public ingress and use private endpoints for control plane traffic.
[00:40] Elena Ruiz: can you spell out the network boundary? like what sits in our VPC vs redwood-managed subnets? we need to map that to our firewall zones.
[00:52] Priya Nanduri: yes good q. typical pattern: control plane connectors (lightweight) can be run in a dedicated management subnet; inference workers sit in private subnets with no public IPs; we recommend NAT for outbound egress, and a small bastion/jump host in a hardened mgmt subnet for ops. we use service endpoints and private link equivalents for telemetry. sometimes folks put a reverse proxy in the DMZ if they want to terminate TLS there.
[01:15] Samir Patel: about ingress - we cannot have inbound from internet to the model nodes, full stop. how do you handle requests from our app servers?
[01:25] Jordan Lee: we provide a private endpoint (mTLS optional) that your app tier talks to over internal network. you can front the endpoint with your ALB/NLB with internal IPs only. we also support VPC peering or Transit Gateway if you have many VPCs.
[01:38] Jill O'Connor: and egress — where do outbound connections go? our compliance team is strict about outbound flows to third party endpoints.
[01:47] Priya Nanduri: good point. Redwood runtime only needs outbound to a few well-defined destinations: control plane telemetry (if you use our control plane), container image registries (or we can mirror images), metrics endpoints, and optionally updates. for strictly air-gapped customers we support fully offline image pushes and private artifact repos. in normal private setup we recommend routing egress through your proxy/NAT and applying egress firewall rules to restrict to our publishing IPs or endpoints.
[02:12] Mark Thompson: is there a published IP list? our security team hates wildcard egress.
[02:18] Jordan Lee: yes we publish a CIDR/IP list for dedicated/private deployments; it's updated in the onboarding repo. we also support DNS-based allowlists and mTLS to further restrict.
[02:28] Elena Ruiz: on firewalling, do you use security groups or iptables inside the worker images?
[02:33] Priya Nanduri: we rely on cloud security groups/nacls as primary. inside the nodes we run a minimal host firewall and processes are constrained; we avoid depending on iptables rules for perimeter security. for on-prem or custom kernel needs we can work with your ops to add host-level hardening.
[02:50] Speaker 1: (overlap) i had a quick question around network logging - do you emit flow logs?
[02:55] Priya Nanduri: yes. VPC flow logs available, and we forward agent logs, app logs, and runtime audit logs to your SIEM. most customers ship to Splunk/Datadog/Elastic via our log forwarding connectors. retention and access control are controlled by you.
[03:12] Samir Patel: let's talk encryption — KMS for data at rest, and TLS for transport. do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in our KMS/HSM?
[03:22] Jordan Lee: yes, we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) for envelope encryption. you can use CMKs and we can optionally use an HSM-backed key for root-level secrets. key rotation handled per your policy; we provide tooling for re-wrapping model artifacts when needed.
[03:36] Mark Thompson: who holds the signing keys for model artifacts?
[03:39] Priya Nanduri: by default Redwood holds the signing keys for our managed model delivery. for higher security we can do a BYOK flow where you sign or host the signing material in your HSM and we verify on deploy. it's part of the private onboarding checklist.
[03:52] Elena Ruiz: audit logs — we need immutable logs for a 7 year retention for certain event classes. is that possible?
[03:59] Priya Nanduri: we support long-term export to your storage (S3/GCS) or to a log archive; we can also write audit events to an append-only store. retention is customer-configurable; the export mechanism ensures you keep the raw events. note: longer retention impacts storage costs on your side.
[04:20] Jill O'Connor: curious about RBAC and SSO — we use Okta and SCIM. can we map our groups to redwood roles and enforce least privilege?
[04:29] Jordan Lee: yes, we support SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC maps to your groups and we can sync role assignments. for private deployments you can host the RBAC control plane in your account for fully isolated auth decisions.
[04:42] Samir Patel: legal will ask about audit trail for admin actions and who can access logs. what granularity do you provide?
[04:49] Priya Nanduri: every operator action is logged with actor, timestamp and operation. we can push those logs to your SIEM and tag them for easy filtering. for redundancy we also keep a secondary log copy in a customer-owned bucket if you want.
[05:05] Jordan Lee: quick note on shared responsibility: Redwood is responsible for the runtime code and secure defaults; customer is responsible for VPC network controls, KMS key custody (if using CMK), firewall rules, and access to their own SIEM and storage. we'll provide a runbook and checklist.
[05:20] Mark Thompson: can you walk through a sample deployment diagram?
[05:24] Priya Nanduri: sure — show diagram link: https://redwood.example/onboarding/vpc-sample (note: link is redwood-hosted repo). diagram explanation: external app tier in app VPC -> peered to redwood worker VPC via Transit Gateway -> internal ALB -> private endpoints -> worker nodes in private subnets -> NAT for restricted egress -> logs to your log-collector in a logging VPC.
[05:48] Elena Ruiz: transit gateway adds cost and complexity; could we use interface VPC endpoints instead?
[05:52] Priya Nanduri: absolutely, interface endpoints (private link) work well for single-region setups. transit gateway helps if you have many VPCs or cross-region routing needs.
[06:04] Jordan Lee: on the topic of performance: bringing nodes into your VPC reduces network hops but we still tune kernel and NIC for high throughput; expect similar latency to hosted but with isolation benefits.
[06:16] Speaker 2: a dumb question — do you need full admin in our account to deploy?
[06:20] Priya Nanduri: no, we recommend using a deployment role with scoped permissions. we provide an IAM role/template with least privilege. we can do a deployment via CI pipeline or via terraform with a role assumption during onboarding.
[06:33] Samir Patel: about DMZ — can we force TLS termination at our edge and do mTLS to the workers?
[06:38] Priya Nanduri: yes. you can terminate TLS at your ALB and use mTLS between ALB and workers. we also support client cert verification and token-based auth.
[06:50] Mark Thompson: for compliance, we want proof of SOC2 and ISO. i assume you have artifacts?
[06:56] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 summary. i'll put those in the onboarding folder.
[07:03] Elena Ruiz: about egress filtering — can you provide a manifest of domains and IPs for your runtime?
[07:09] Jordan Lee: yes we publish an allowlist and a change log. we can also support DAAS style manifest for strict lock-down.
[07:16] Jill O'Connor: log forwarding — we run their SIEM in a private subnet with no public endpoint. can you talk to an on-prem collector?
[07:24] Priya Nanduri: we can forward via private link to your logging VPC or use a collector in your network; for on-prem we can use a secure relay over a TLS tunnel to your collector.
[07:36] Samir Patel: HSM options — if we want FIPS 140-2/HSM-backed keys, how does that work?
[07:42] Priya Nanduri: you can keep keys in your HSM and use envelope encryption. Redwood will never hold plaintext root keys. we integrate with customer HSMs for signing if needed. for air-gapped setups we provide an offline key import workflow.
[07:56] Jordan Lee: let's touch on our incident response playbook — we provide runbooks and a contact path. we can run joint exercises and provide playbooks for data exfil, node compromise, etc.
[08:06] Mark Thompson: that would be helpful. can you also provide RTO/RPO guidance for the private deployment?
[08:12] Priya Nanduri: yes typical RTO for a node replacement is a few minutes; overall service-level RTO depends on your HA config and cross-zone deployment. we'll include suggested HA patterns in the runbook.
[08:24] Elena Ruiz: any network-level intrusion detection?
[08:28] Priya Nanduri: we emit telemetry and can integrate with your IDS/IPS. some customers run eBPF-based monitoring on hosts for additional telemetry; we can support that during onboarding.
[08:40] Speaker 3: i saw mention of KV cache earlier in your docs — any risk of in-memory leakage across tenants?
[08:47] Priya Nanduri: in private deployment there is single-tenant capacity by default, but our runtime still prevents KV leakage via strict partitioning and memory zeroing on recycling; we also recommend pinning models per-tenant to avoid shared caches.
[09:01] Jordan Lee: let me summarize next steps and responsibilities...
[09:05] Jordan Lee: Jordan -> send SOC2/ISO and network diagram; Priya -> terraform templates, sample security group/NACL rules, and egress allowlist; customer -> share firewall baseline and schedule connectivity test.
[09:18] Mark Thompson: that works. any blockers for us to start a pilot? costs and timeline?
[09:23] Jordan Lee: pilot timeline usually 2-4 weeks for onboarding + validation depending on your change window. cost for private deployment is a combination of reserved capacity + infra costs in your account. we'll share pricing in the follow-up.
[09:37] Elena Ruiz: small nit - do you support private DNS for endpoints? we have split-horizon DNS.
[09:42] Priya Nanduri: yes split-horizon/private hosted zone support is common. we provide DNS entries that resolve to internal IPs in your VPC.
[09:51] Jill O'Connor: about firewall rules, do you recommend security groups only or security groups + NACL?
[09:57] Priya Nanduri: security groups for instance-level controls, NACLs for subnet-level enforced policies; we usually give both patterns in the template.
[10:07] Samir Patel: are there any managed connectors that require outbound to SaaS? we prefer to avoid cross-border data flows.
[10:12] Jordan Lee: all control-plane telemetry can be optional. you can disable telemetry egress or route it through your collector. data residency is respected — you can host everything in-region or on-prem.
[10:24] Speaker 1: any recommended firewall rules for SSH and admin access?
[10:28] Priya Nanduri: restrict SSH to jump host only, use ephemeral bastion sessions, enforce MFA, and log sessions to your session manager. use ephemeral keys where possible.
[10:39] Mark Thompson: what about secret management for runtime — do you recommend putting secrets in our vault and injecting at startup?
[10:46] Priya Nanduri: yes use your vault/KMS and short-lived tokens. we support fetching secrets at startup and caching in memory only; we avoid persistent plaintext on disk.
[10:56] Jordan Lee: quick check — does silver lake have any regulatory constraints that mandate on-prem deployment?
[11:01] Mark Thompson: some of our regulated lines prefer on-prem or air-gapped, but initially we'd like private VPC in our cloud region; if it gets to production for certain business lines we may request an on-prem pack.
[11:12] Priya Nanduri: we have an on-prem package that mirrors the private deployment but with additional offline workflows and no egress. it's heavier but supported.
[11:22] Elena Ruiz: can you provide a sample firewall rule set and the order of operations when onboarding?
[11:27] Jordan Lee: yes we'll provide a checklist: 1) create onboarding role & least-priv IAM, 2) apply VPC subnets and security groups from template, 3) deploy control plane connectors, 4) validate connectivity, 5) run perf/latency tests, 6) enable audit exports.
[11:44] Speaker 2: any questions about cert management?
[11:46] Priya Nanduri: we support both operator-managed certs and customer-managed certs via ACME or manual import. for mTLS we can rotate certs automatically if you allow a cert-rotation role.
[11:58] Samir Patel: ok, last thing — can we get a signed BA or DPA?
[12:02] Jordan Lee: yes BA/DPA can be shared; legal will coordinate. i'll loop in our contracts specialist.
[12:10] Jordan Lee: that's the core of it, thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[12:15] Mark Thompson: thanks everyone, appreciated.
[12:18] End of call (approx 56 minutes)

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings and speaker attribution may be imperfect. References: onboarding repo link (redwood.example/onboarding/vpc-sample), SOC2-artifact placeholder (redwood.example/security/soc2). Recap in transcript aligned with metadata next steps and action items.
